title.en: Volume 323 Biographies 82: Yu Zhaomin, Gao Hua, Zhou Mei, Yan Shougong, Meng Yuan, Liu Qian, Zhao Zhen, Zhang Zhong, Fan Ke, Ma Huaide, An Jun, Xiang Bao
title.raw: 卷三百二十三 列傳第八十二 蔚昭敏 高化 周美 閻守恭 孟元 劉謙 趙振 張忠 范恪 馬懷德 安俊 向寶 Volume 323 Biographies 82: Yu Zhaomin, Gao Hua, Zhou Mei, Yan Shougong, Meng Yuan, Liu Qian, Zhao Zhen, Zhang Zhong, Fan Ke, Ma Huaide, An Jun, Xiang Bao

sentences.zh: 蔚昭敏

translations.literal: Yu Zhaomin
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhaomin

sentences.zh: 蔚昭敏，字仲明，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Yu Zhaomin, styled Zhongming, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhaomin, whose courtesy name was Zhongming, came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父興，事周世宗，數戰伐有功，又從太宗平太原，終龍尉都虞候。

translations.literal: His father Xing served Emperor Shizong of Zhou, won merit in many campaigns, also followed Taizong in pacifying Taiyuan, and ended as Chief Commandant of the Dragon Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xing had served Emperor Shizong of Zhou, distinguishing himself in repeated campaigns, and later followed Taizong in the pacification of Taiyuan; he ended his career as chief commandant of the Dragon Guards.

sentences.zh: 真宗為襄王，昭敏自東班殿侍選隸襄王府。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was Prince of Xiang, Zhaomin was chosen from the Eastern Class palace attendants to serve in the prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhenzong was still Prince of Xiang, Zhaomin was selected from the Eastern Class palace attendants and assigned to the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，授西頭供奉官，累遷崇儀使、冀貝行營兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he was appointed Western Head Palace Attendant, and was promoted in succession to Honored Ceremonial Envoy and Military Superintendent of the Ji and Bei circuit encampments.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's accession he was made Western Head Palace Attendant, and rose in turn to Honored Ceremonial Envoy and military superintendent of the Ji and Bei field encampments.

sentences.zh: 契丹以五千騎突至冀州城南，昭敏帥部兵與戰，敗之，得其器甲，賊遁去，而師不失一人。

translations.literal: The Khitan with five thousand horsemen suddenly reached south of Jizhou; Zhaomin led his troops to fight, defeated them, seized their armor and weapons, the bandits fled, and not a single man of his army was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When five thousand Khitan horsemen suddenly appeared south of Jizhou, Zhaomin led his troops into battle, routed them, and captured their arms and armor; the enemy fled, and his force did not lose a single man.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，領順州刺史、定州行營鈐轄兼押大陣，又為鎮、定、高陽關三路先鋒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he was made prefect of Shunzhou, Commandant of the Dingzhou field headquarters with charge of the main battle array, and also vanguard of the three routes of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping he held the prefecture of Shun, served as commandant of the Dingzhou field headquarters with charge of the main array, and was also vanguard for the three routes of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，帝北巡至大名，契丹退趨莫州，昭敏與范廷召追至莫州東三十里，斬首萬餘級，擒生口甚眾，契丹委器甲遁去。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, the emperor went north on inspection to Daming; the Khitan withdrew toward Mozhou. Zhaomin and Fan Tingzhao pursued them thirty li east of Mozhou, beheaded more than ten thousand, captured many prisoners alive, and the Khitan abandoned their armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: During a Khitan invasion the emperor toured north as far as Daming; when the Khitan fell back toward Mozhou, Zhaomin and Fan Tingzhao pursued them thirty li east of Mozhou, took more than ten thousand heads, captured a great many prisoners, and the Khitan abandoned their arms and armor in flight.

sentences.zh: 拜唐州團練使，累遷至殿前副都指揮使，遷都指揮使、保靜軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Training Commissioner of Tang Prefecture, promoted in succession to Deputy Director-in-Chief of the Palace Front Corps, then Director-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military training commissioner of Tang Prefecture, rose in succession to deputy director-in-chief of the Palace Front Corps, and was then promoted to director-in-chief and military commissioner of Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 以足疾，命入謁無拜。

translations.literal: Because of foot ailment, he was ordered to attend audience without bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a foot ailment he was permitted to attend court without performing the full bow.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 高化，字仲熙，真定人。

translations.literal: Gao Hua, styled Zhongxi, was a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hua, whose courtesy name was Zhongxi, came from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 少沉勇有力，不事耕稼，學擊劍，善射。

translations.literal: In youth he was calm, brave, and strong, did not farm, studied swordsmanship, and was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was steady, courageous, and strong; he did not work the fields but studied swordplay and became an expert archer.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯河北，應募轉餉飛狐口。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded Hebei, he enlisted to transport supplies to Feihu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided Hebei, he volunteered to haul provisions to Feihu Pass.

sentences.zh: 楊業留戲下，使捕賊酋大鵬翼，獲之。

translations.literal: Yang Ye kept him in his command and had him capture the bandit chieftain Da Pengyi, which he did.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye kept him in his service and sent him to capture the rebel chieftain Da Pengyi, whom he took alive.

sentences.zh: 會契丹又犯真定，乃辭業還家，家屬盡為契丹所掠去。

translations.literal: When the Khitan again invaded Zhending, he bade Yang Ye farewell and returned home; his entire household was carried off by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan again struck Zhending, he left Yang Ye's service and went home, only to find his whole family carried off by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 從州將入京師，遂隸禁軍，選為襄王牽䪊官。

translations.literal: He followed the prefectural commander to the capital, then entered the palace guards, and was selected as horse-leader for the Prince of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed a prefectural commander to the capital, entered the palace guards, and was chosen as horse-leader for the Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 王尹京，命巡內外八廂，積獲奸盜甚眾。

translations.literal: When the prince governed the capital, he was ordered to patrol the eight wards inside and out, and accumulated many captured criminals.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince served as capital intendant, Hua was ordered to patrol the eight inner and outer wards and over time seized a great many thieves and rogues.

sentences.zh: 盜有遺化金帛者，化弗受。

translations.literal: When robbers left gold and silk for Hua, he would not take it.
translations.idiomatic: When captured robbers left him gold and silk, he refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 一日，王趨急召出府門，馬驚墮，化掖之而起。

translations.literal: One day the prince was urgently summoned out the mansion gate; his horse shied and threw him, and Hua helped him up.
translations.idiomatic: One day the prince was summoned in haste out the mansion gate; his horse bolted and threw him, and Hua steadied him and helped him rise.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「微爾。

translations.literal: The prince said: "But for you—
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "But for you—

sentences.zh: 吾幾殆。

translations.literal: I was nearly killed."
translations.idiomatic: I would have been killed."

sentences.zh: 」益親信之。

translations.literal: He trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the prince relied on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 發兵襲明珠族，不利，降滑州總管。

translations.literal: He raised troops to attack the Mingzhu tribe, met with no success, and surrendered to the Huazhou military superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops against the Mingzhu tribe, met defeat, and submitted to the Huazhou military superintendent.

sentences.zh: 改興州防禦使、真定路副都總管，徙高陽關路。

translations.literal: He was changed to Defender of Xing Prefecture and Deputy Chief Commander of the Zhending circuit, then transferred to the Gaoyang Pass circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed defender of Xing Prefecture and deputy chief commander of the Zhending circuit, then transferred to the Gaoyang Pass circuit.

sentences.zh: 修護章惠太后園陵，累拜殿前副都指揮使，歷建武軍節度使。

translations.literal: He oversaw the mausoleum park of Empress Zhanghui, was repeatedly promoted to Deputy Director-in-Chief of the Palace Front Corps, and served as Military Commissioner of Jianwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised repairs at Empress Zhanghui's mausoleum park, rose in succession to deputy director-in-chief of the Palace Front Corps, and served as military commissioner of Jianwu Army.

sentences.zh: 以老，辭管軍。

translations.literal: Because of old age he resigned from command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew old he resigned from army command.

sentences.zh: 詔入朝，化又固請，改武安軍節度使、知滄州，未行，改相州。

translations.literal: He was ordered to court, but Hua again firmly petitioned; he was changed to Military Commissioner of Wu'an Army and made prefect of Cangzhou, but before departing was changed to Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him to court, but Hua petitioned again; he was made military commissioner of Wu'an Army and prefect of Cangzhou, yet before he set out was reassigned to Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 部有大獄已具，皆當論死。

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction a major case had been concluded with all condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: In his jurisdiction a major case had already been concluded, with every defendant sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 化疑之，遣移訊，果出無罪者三人。

translations.literal: Hua had doubts, sent it for reinvestigation, and indeed three innocent persons were released.
translations.idiomatic: Hua had doubts, ordered the case reinvestigated elsewhere, and three innocent men were indeed released.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復告老，以右屯衛上將軍致仕。

translations.literal: After a year he again reported old age and retired as General-in-Chief of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he again pleaded old age and retired with the rank of general-in-chief of the Right Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，諡曰恭莊。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Marshal, posthumous title Gongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal with the posthumous title Gongzhuang (Respectful and Dignified).

sentences.zh: 化謹質少過，馭軍有法。

translations.literal: Hua was cautious and plain with few faults, and governed the army by rule.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was careful and unassuming, rarely at fault, and governed his troops by strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 雖起身行伍，然頗知民事焉。

translations.literal: Though he rose from the ranks, he was quite knowledgeable about civilian affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had risen from the ranks, he was well versed in civilian affairs.

sentences.zh: 周美，字之純，靈州回樂人。

translations.literal: Zhou Mei, styled Zhichun, was a man of Huile in Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mei, whose courtesy name was Zhichun, came from Huile in Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少隸朔方軍，以材武稱。

translations.literal: In youth he served in the Shuofang Army and was famed for talent and martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served in the Shuofang Army and won renown for ability and valor.

sentences.zh: 趙保吉陷靈州，美棄其族，間走歸京師，天子召見，隸禁軍。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baoji seized Ling Prefecture, Mei abandoned his clan, stole away to the capital, was summoned by the Son of Heaven, and entered the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baoji took Ling Prefecture, Mei left his kinsmen behind, made his way secretly to the capital, was received in audience by the emperor, and was enrolled in the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯邊，真宗幸澶州，禦城北門，美慷慨自陳，願假數騎縛契丹將至闕下，帝壯之，常令宿衛。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided the frontier, Zhenzong went to Chanyuan and inspected the north gate of the city; Mei spoke boldly on his own behalf, asking for a few horsemen to bind a Khitan general and bring him to the palace, and the emperor admired his spirit and often had him on night guard.
translations.idiomatic: During a Khitan border raid Zhenzong went to Chanyuan and reviewed troops at the city's north gate; Mei stepped forward boldly and offered, with only a few horsemen, to seize a Khitan general and bring him bound to court. The emperor was impressed and regularly kept him on palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，德明部落寇平涼方渠，美以軍候戍邊，與州將追戰，破之於九井原、烏侖河，斬首甚眾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, Deming's tribes raided Pingliang and Fangqu; Mei served on the frontier as army scout, pursued with the prefectural commander, and defeated them at Jiujing Plain and Wulun River, beheading a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiansheng era, Deming's tribes raided Pingliang and Fangqu; Mei was posted to the frontier as army scout, joined the prefectural commander in pursuit, and routed them at Jiujing Plain and on the Wulun River, taking many heads.

sentences.zh: 累遷天武都虞候。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Commandant of the Heavenly Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to commandant of the Heavenly Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，陝西用兵，經略使夏竦薦其材，擢供備庫使、延州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled and Shaanxi saw military action, Frontier Commissioner Xia Song recommended his ability; he was promoted to Commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Repository and Military Superintendent of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled and war broke out in Shaanxi, frontier commissioner Xia Song recommended his talent; he was promoted to commissioner of the supply and equipment repository and military superintendent of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏人既破金明諸砦，美請於經略使范仲淹曰：「夏人新得志，其勢必復來。

translations.literal: After the Xia had taken the Jinming forts, Mei petitioned Frontier Commissioner Fan Zhongyan, saying: "The Xia have just gained their wish; they are sure to come again.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xia had overrun the Jinming forts, Mei urged frontier commissioner Fan Zhongyan: "The Xia have just tasted victory; they are certain to return.

sentences.zh: 金明當邊衝，我之蔽也，今不亟完，將遂失之。

translations.literal: Jinming stands on the frontier pass; it is our screen. If we do not repair it at once, we shall lose it for good.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming lies on the frontier choke point—it is our shield. If we do not repair it immediately, we shall lose it altogether.

sentences.zh: 」仲淹因屬美復城如故。

translations.literal: " Zhongyan therefore entrusted Mei to restore the fort as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongyan accordingly entrusted Mei with restoring the fort to its former state.

sentences.zh: 數日賊果來，其眾數萬薄金明，陣於延安城北三十里。

translations.literal: Within days the bandits indeed came; their force of tens of thousands pressed Jinming and formed battle lines thirty li north of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the enemy did come: tens of thousands pressed Jinming and drew up in battle order thirty li north of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 美領眾二千力戰，抵暮，援兵不至，乃徙軍山北，多設疑兵。

translations.literal: Mei led two thousand men in fierce fighting until evening; reinforcements did not arrive, so he moved his army north of the mountain and set out many decoy forces.
translations.idiomatic: Mei led two thousand men in hard fighting until evening; when no reinforcements came, he shifted his troops north of the hill and deployed many decoys.

sentences.zh: 夏人望見，以為救至，即引去。

translations.literal: The Xia saw them, thought relief had arrived, and withdrew at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia saw them, took them for arriving relief, and withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 既而復出艾蒿砦，遂至郭北平，夜鬥不解。

translations.literal: Soon after they came out again from Aigao Fort, reaching Guobei Plain, and fought through the night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: They soon sallied again from Aigao Fort, reached Guobei Plain, and fought through the night without letup.

sentences.zh: 美率眾使人持一炬從間道上山，益張旗幟，四面大噪，賊懼走。

translations.literal: Mei led his men, had men carry torches up a hidden path, spread banners still more widely, raised a great clamor on all sides, and the bandits fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Mei led his force, sent men with torches up a concealed path, unfurled still more banners, and raised a deafening uproar on every side until the enemy fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 獲牛羊、橐駝、鎧甲數千計，遂募兵築萬安城而還。

translations.literal: They seized cattle, sheep, camels, and armor by the thousands, then recruited troops, built Wan'an Fort, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They captured thousands of cattle, sheep, camels, and suits of armor, then raised troops, built Wan'an Fort, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 敵復寇金明，美引兵由虞家堡並北山而下，敵即引卻。

translations.literal: The enemy again raided Jinming; Mei led troops down from Yujia Fort along the north mountain, and the enemy withdrew at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy raided Jinming again, Mei led his troops down from Yujia Fort along the northern hills, and the enemy withdrew immediately.

sentences.zh: 遷文思使，徙知保定軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Literary Accomplishment Envoy and moved to govern Baoding Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Literary Accomplishment Envoy and transferred to govern Baoding Army.

sentences.zh: 經略使龐籍表留之，改東路都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Frontier Commissioner Pang Ji memorialized to keep him and changed him to Eastern Route Chief Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commissioner Pang Ji memorialized to retain him, and he was made chief inspector of the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 敗敵於金湯城，焚其族部二十一。

translations.literal: He defeated the enemy at Jintang Fort and burned twenty-one of their tribal encampments.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the enemy at Jintang Fort and burned twenty-one of their tribal settlements.

sentences.zh: 元昊大入，據承平砦。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao invaded in force and seized Chengpu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao launched a major invasion and occupied Chengpu Fort.

sentences.zh: 諸將會兵議攻討，洛苑副使种世衡請齎三日糧直搗敵穴。

translations.literal: The generals gathered troops to discuss an attack; Vice Commissioner of Luoyuan Park Zhong Shihang asked to carry three days' rations and strike straight at the enemy's lair.
translations.idiomatic: The generals assembled to plan an assault; Vice Commissioner of Luoyuan Park Zhong Shihang proposed carrying three days' rations and driving straight at the enemy stronghold.

sentences.zh: 美曰：「彼知吾來，必設伏待我。

translations.literal: Mei said: "If they know we are coming, they are sure to set ambushes to wait for us.
translations.idiomatic: Mei said, "Once they know we are coming, they are certain to lay ambushes for us.

sentences.zh: 不如間道掩其不意。

translations.literal: Better to take a hidden route and strike where they do not expect.
translations.idiomatic: Better to take a concealed route and strike where they do not expect us.

sentences.zh: 」世衡不聽。

translations.literal: " Shihang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Shihang would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 美獨以兵西出芙蓉谷，大破敵。

translations.literal: Mei alone led troops west out through Furong Valley and routed the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Mei alone marched west through Furong Valley with his troops and inflicted a crushing defeat on the enemy.

sentences.zh: 世衡等果無功。

translations.literal: Shihang and the others indeed achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Shihang and his colleagues, as expected, achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，敵復略土塠砦，美迎擊於野家店，追北至拓跋谷，大敗其眾。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy again raided Tudun Fort; Mei met them at Yejia Inn, pursued north to the Tuoba Valley, and routed their force.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy raided Tudun Fort again; Mei met them at Yejia Inn, pursued north to Tuoba Valley, and routed their army.

sentences.zh: 以功遷右騏驥使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Right Qiji Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to Right Qiji Envoy.

sentences.zh: 軍還，築柵於蔥梅官道谷，以據敵路。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he built palisades in Congmei Official Road Valley to block the enemy route.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he built palisades in Congmei Official Road Valley to hold the enemy's line of advance.

sentences.zh: 令士卒益種營田，而收穀六千斛。

translations.literal: He ordered the soldiers to plant more garrison fields and harvested six thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He had the troops expand garrison farming and harvested six thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 復率眾繇廳子部西濟大理河，屠劄萬多移二百帳，焚其積聚以歸。

translations.literal: Again he led his force west from Tingzi tribe, crossed the Dali River, slaughtered two hundred tents of Zhawanduoyi, burned their stores, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He again led his troops west from the Tingzi tribe, crossed the Dali River, destroyed two hundred tents of the Zhawanduoyi, burned their stockpiles, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 籍、仲淹交薦之，除鄜延路兵馬都監，遷賀州刺史。

translations.literal: Ji and Zhongyan jointly recommended him; he was appointed Military Superintendent of the Fuyan circuit and promoted to prefect of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Zhongyan both recommended him; he was made military superintendent of the Fuyan circuit and promoted to prefect of He.

sentences.zh: 初，美自靈武來，上其所服精甲，詔藏軍器庫。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mei came from Lingwu, he presented the fine armor he wore, and an edict ordered it stored in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: When Mei first came from Lingwu he had presented the fine armor he wore, and an edict ordered it kept in the armory.

sentences.zh: 至是，加飾黃金，遣使即軍中賜之。

translations.literal: At this time gold ornament was added, and an envoy was sent to bestow it on him in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Now gold ornament was added, and an envoy was sent to present it to him in camp.

sentences.zh: 又破敵於無定河，乘勝至綏州，殺其酋豪，焚廬帳，獲牛馬、羊駝、器械三百計，因城龍口平砦。

translations.literal: Again he defeated the enemy on the Wuding River, pressed the victory to Sui Prefecture, killed their chieftains, burned their tents, seized some three hundred head of cattle, horses, sheep, camels, and sets of equipment, and thereupon fortified Longkouping Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He again routed the enemy on the Wuding River, pressed on to Sui Prefecture, killed their tribal leaders, burned their camps, and captured some three hundred head of cattle, horses, sheep, camels, and sets of equipment, then fortified Longkouping Fort.

sentences.zh: 敵以精騎數千來襲，美從百餘騎馳擊破之。

translations.literal: The enemy came to attack with several thousand elite horsemen; Mei with a little over a hundred horsemen charged and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When several thousand elite enemy horsemen attacked, Mei with a little over a hundred riders charged and broke them.

sentences.zh: 加本路鈐轄，遂為副總管。

translations.literal: He was given additional charge as circuit commandant and then became deputy chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commandant of the circuit and then deputy chief commander.

sentences.zh: 遷龍神衛四廂都指揮使、通州刺史；

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director-in-Chief of the four wings of the Dragon Divine Guards and prefect of Tong Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director-in-chief of the four wings of the Dragon Divine Guards and prefect of Tong Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 進捧日、天武四廂都指揮使，陵州團練使。

translations.literal: advanced to Director-in-Chief of the four wings of the Sun-Bearing and Heavenly Martial Guards, and Military Training Commissioner of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: then advanced to director-in-chief of the four wings of the Sun-Bearing and Heavenly Martial Guards and military training commissioner of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，又城清水、安定、黑水、佛堂、北橫山、乾谷、土明、柳谷、雕巢、盧兒、原安砦十一堡。

translations.literal: During Qingli he also fortified eleven forts: Qingshui, Anding, Heishui, Fotang, North Hengshan, Gangu, Tuming, Liugu, Diaochao, Lu'er, and Yuan'an.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era he also fortified eleven strongpoints: Qingshui, Anding, Heishui, Fotang, North Hengshan, Gangu, Tuming, Liugu, Diaochao, Lu'er, and Yuan'an.

sentences.zh: 安定之役，諜報敵數萬將大至，經略使遣管勾機宜楚建中分諸將兵，趣城黑水以待。

translations.literal: In the Anding campaign, spies reported that tens of thousands of the enemy were about to arrive in force; the frontier commissioner sent Staff Officer Chu Jianzhong to divide the generals' troops and hurry to fortify Heishui to await them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Anding campaign, intelligence reported that tens of thousands of the enemy were about to arrive; the frontier commissioner sent staff officer Chu Jianzhong to apportion the generals' forces and rush to fortify Heishui in anticipation.

sentences.zh: 諸將憚敵且至，不肯與兵。

translations.literal: The generals feared the enemy was about to arrive and would not give him troops.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, fearing the enemy's imminent arrival, refused to furnish him troops.

sentences.zh: 美曰：「兵常以寡擊眾，何自怯也。

translations.literal: Mei said: "Soldiers often use the few to strike the many—why be timid yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: Mei said, "Soldiers are meant to strike many with few—why shrink from it?

sentences.zh: 」卒以兵二千與建中，而敵亦引去。

translations.literal: " In the end he gave Jianzhong two thousand troops, and the enemy also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he furnished Jianzhong with two thousand troops, and the enemy withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 每邊書至，諸將各擇便利，獨美未嘗辭難，然所向輒克，諸將以此服之。

translations.literal: Whenever frontier dispatches arrived, each general chose what was convenient; only Mei never declined hardship, yet wherever he went he prevailed, and the generals for this reason submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever frontier dispatches arrived, the other generals each chose the easier assignment; Mei alone never shirked hardship, yet wherever he went he prevailed, and for this the generals respected him.

sentences.zh: 歷侍衛親軍馬軍殿前都虞候、眉州防禦使、步軍副都指揮使、遂州觀察使、鄜延副都總管。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Commandant of the Palace Cavalry and Palace Front Corps of the Imperial Guards, Defender of Meizhou, Deputy Director-in-Chief of the Foot Guards, Observation Commissioner of Suizhou, and Deputy Chief Commander of Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to commandant of the palace cavalry and Palace Front Corps of the imperial guards, defender of Meizhou, deputy director-in-chief of the foot guards, observation commissioner of Suizhou, and deputy chief commander of Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 召還，授耀州觀察使，又進馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was recalled and given the post of Observation Commissioner of Yao Prefecture, then advanced to Deputy Director-in-Chief of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled, appointed observation commissioner of Yao Prefecture, and then promoted to deputy director-in-chief of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈忠武軍節度使，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Military Commissioner of Zhongwu Army, posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as military commissioner of Zhongwu Army with the posthumous title Zhongyi (Loyal and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 自陝西用兵，諸將多不利，美前後十餘戰，平族帳二百，焚二十一，招種落內附者十一族，復城堡甚多。

translations.literal: Since military action in Shaanxi, most generals had fared poorly; Mei in more than ten battles before and after pacified two hundred tribal tents, burned twenty-one, induced eleven tribes to submit inward, and recovered many forts and castles.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Shaanxi campaigns began, most generals had fared poorly; Mei fought more than ten engagements in all, pacified two hundred tribal encampments, burned twenty-one, brought eleven tribes to submit, and recovered a great many forts and strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 在軍中所得祿賜，多分其戲下，有餘，悉饗勞之。

translations.literal: The salary and gifts he received in the army he largely divided among his subordinates; what remained he entirely used to feast and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: He gave most of his salary and gifts in the army to his men; whatever remained he spent entirely on feasts to reward them.

sentences.zh: 及死，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: When he died, the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his household had nothing left in reserve.

sentences.zh: 子蚤卒，以孫永清為子，官至引進副使。

translations.literal: His son died young; he took his grandson Yongqing as son, who reached the post of Vice Introducing Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: His son died young; he adopted his grandson Yongqing, who rose to vice introducing envoy.

sentences.zh: 閻守恭

translations.literal: Yan Shougong
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shougong

sentences.zh: 閻守恭，并州榆次人。

translations.literal: Yan Shougong was a man of Yuci in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shougong came from Yuci in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父榮，倜儻有志略，劉繼元欲召至帳下，辭以母老不就。

translations.literal: His father Rong was bold and free-spirited with ambition and stratagem; Liu Jiyuan wished to summon him to his staff, but he declined on the ground that his mother was old and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rong was bold and enterprising; Liu Jiyuan wished to recruit him to his staff, but he declined on the plea that his mother was elderly and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 守恭生而體貌奇偉，榮曰：「是必當事太平天子，吾無恨矣。

translations.literal: Shougong was born with an extraordinary stature; Rong said: "This one is sure to serve the Son of Heaven in an age of peace; I shall have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Shougong was born with an imposing physique; Rong said, "This boy is destined to serve the Son of Heaven in an age of peace; I shall have no regrets.

sentences.zh: 」後十七年，劉氏平，徙太原民於大名府，因家焉。

translations.literal: " Seventeen years later the Liu house was pacified; the people of Taiyuan were moved to Daming Prefecture, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: " Seventeen years later the Liu regime fell; the people of Taiyuan were relocated to Daming Prefecture, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 往來負販於並、汾間，過西山，聞郭進為都巡檢使，太宗甚寵遇之。

translations.literal: Going back and forth as a peddler between Bing and Fen, he passed the Western Hills and heard that Guo Jin was Chief Inspector and that Taizong greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled as a peddler between Bing and Fen; passing the Western Hills he heard that Guo Jin was chief inspector and that Taizong greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 乃慨然曰：「進不遇主，亦行伍爾，吾自度豈不及進邪？

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "Had Jin not met his lord, he too would be only a soldier in the ranks—when I measure myself, am I not Jin's equal?
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "Had Jin not found his sovereign, he too would be nothing but a common soldier—why should I not measure up to Jin?

sentences.zh: 」遂應募，隸拱聖軍，擢殿前押班。

translations.literal: " He then enlisted, entered the Palatine Sacred Army, and was promoted to Palace Front Escort Leader.
translations.idiomatic: " He then enlisted, joined the Palatine Sacred Army, and was promoted to palace front escort leader.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，從幸河北，以功為捧日副指揮使，歷拱聖、龍衛、捧日指揮使，累遷左第二軍指揮使、乾州刺史。

translations.literal: During Xianping he followed the emperor's tour to Hebei; for merit he became Deputy Commander of the Sun-Bearing Guards, served in succession as commander of the Palatine Sacred, Dragon Guards, and Sun-Bearing Guards, and was promoted in succession to Commander of the Left Second Army and prefect of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping he accompanied the emperor to Hebei; for his achievements he became deputy commander of the Sun-Bearing Guards, served in turn as commander of the Palatine Sacred, Dragon Guards, and Sun-Bearing Guards, and rose to commander of the Left Second Army and prefect of Qian.

sentences.zh: 明道中，落軍職，以德州刺史為永興軍兵馬鈐轄，徙幷代路。

translations.literal: During Mingdao he was removed from army office, made Military Commandant of Yongxing Army as prefect of Dezhou, and transferred to the Bingdai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During Mingdao he was stripped of his army post, appointed military commandant of Yongxing Army while serving as prefect of Dezhou, and transferred to the Bingdai circuit.

sentences.zh: 守恭性沉勇，御軍嚴。

translations.literal: Shougong was by nature calm and brave and governed the army strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Shougong was calm and courageous by nature and ruled his troops with strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 雖家居如對賓客。

translations.literal: Even at home he was as toward guests.
translations.idiomatic: Even at home he conducted himself as if receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 常訪求士大夫，取郭進事而師法之。

translations.literal: He constantly sought out scholar-officials, took the affairs of Guo Jin, and took them as his model to emulate.
translations.idiomatic: He often sought out scholar-officials and modeled himself on the example of Guo Jin.

sentences.zh: 所得奉祿悉散予人。

translations.literal: All the salary he received he entirely distributed to others.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away all of his salary to others.

sentences.zh: 在并州，因春社會賓客曰：「守恭，太原一貧民爾。

translations.literal: While at Bingzhou, on the occasion of the spring communal sacrifice he addressed his guests, saying: "Shougong is nothing but a poor man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at Bingzhou, he gathered his guests at the spring communal sacrifice and said, "Shougong is nothing but a poor man from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 徒步位刺史，老復官鄉里，逾分多矣。

translations.literal: On foot to the rank of prefect, in old age to hold office again in my hometown — I have exceeded my proper station greatly.
translations.idiomatic: To rise from nothing to the rank of prefect, and in my old age to hold office again in my hometown — I have far exceeded what I deserve.

sentences.zh: 今日與卿輩訣。

translations.literal: Today I take leave of you all.
translations.idiomatic: Today I bid you all farewell.

sentences.zh: 」後十日卒。

translations.literal: " Ten days later he died.
translations.idiomatic: " Ten days later he died.

sentences.zh: 孟元，字善長，洺州人。

translations.literal: Meng Yuan, styled Shanchang, was a native of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yuan, styled Shanchang, came from Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 性謹願少過，頗喜讀書。

translations.literal: By nature cautious and honest with few faults, he quite liked reading books.
translations.idiomatic: He was cautious and upright by nature, seldom at fault, and fond of reading.

sentences.zh: 少隸禁軍，以挽強選補殿侍，累遷散都頭班指揮使，擢如京使、幷代州兵馬都監，改鈐轄，徙高陽關路，又徙真定路。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the Forbidden Army; through strength in drawing the bow he was selected and appointed a palace attendant, was promoted in succession to commander of the scattered company head class, was promoted to Commissioner as if to the Capital and military superintendent of Bing and Dai prefectures, was changed to deputy military commissioner, was transferred to the Gaoyang Gate circuit, and again transferred to the Zhending circuit.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he joined the Forbidden Army and, selected for his strength at drawing the bow, was appointed a palace attendant. He rose through the ranks to command the scattered company head class, was promoted to Commissioner as if to the Capital and military superintendent of Bing and Dai prefectures, served as deputy military commissioner, and was transferred first to the Gaoyang Gate circuit and then to the Zhending circuit.

sentences.zh: 王則據貝州反，元赴城下攻戰，被數十創，又中機石，墜濠中。

translations.literal: Wang Ze seized Beizhou and rebelled; Yuan went to the foot of the city wall to attack and fight, suffered several dozen wounds, was also struck by a catapult stone, and fell into the moat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ze seized Beizhou and rebelled, Yuan fought at the city wall, suffering several dozen wounds; he was also struck by a catapult stone and fell into the moat.

sentences.zh: 既出，戰愈力。

translations.literal: Once he got out, he fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Once he climbed out, he fought all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 更募死士由永濟渠穴地以進。

translations.literal: He recruited dare-to-die soldiers anew and advanced by tunneling underground through the Yongji Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited fresh dare-to-die troops and advanced by tunneling under the Yongji Canal.

sentences.zh: 賊平，改右騏驥使，徙大名府路鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, he was changed to Right Qiji Commissioner and transferred to deputy military commissioner of the Daming Prefecture circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, he was appointed Right Qiji Commissioner and transferred to deputy military commissioner of the Daming Prefecture circuit.

sentences.zh: 河朔饑，權知滄州。

translations.literal: When Hebei suffered famine, he served as acting prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei suffered famine, he served as acting prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 民鬻鹽為生，歲荒鹽多不售，民無以自給。

translations.literal: The people made a living selling salt; in the year of famine much salt would not sell, and the people had no means to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The people made their living selling salt, but in the famine year much of it would not sell, and they had no way to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 元度軍食有餘，悉用易鹽，繇是民不轉徙。

translations.literal: Yuan calculated that military provisions were surplus and used them all to exchange for salt; thereby the people did not migrate elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan saw that the army had surplus provisions and used them all to buy salt, so the people no longer had to flee elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞郭勸言其貝州功而賞未當，乃擢普州刺史，遷宮苑使，專管勾麟府軍馬事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Guo Quan said his Beizhou merit had not been properly rewarded; thereupon he was promoted to prefect of Puzhou, transferred to Palace Parks Commissioner, and put in sole charge of mustering Lin Prefecture army horses.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Guo Quan argued that his merit at Beizhou had not been properly rewarded; he was thereupon promoted to prefect of Puzhou, made Palace Parks Commissioner, and put in sole charge of mustering the army horses of Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 護築永寧堡，敵不敢動。

translations.literal: He protected and built Yongning Fort; the enemy did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the construction of Yongning Fort, and the enemy did not dare stir.

sentences.zh: 為龍神衛四廂都指揮使、忠州團練使、高陽關馬步軍總管，遷天武、捧日四廂都指揮使，又遷步軍都虞候、眉州防禦使、幷代路副都總管。

translations.literal: He served as commander of all four companies of the Dragon Spirit Guard, regimented trainer of Zhongzhou, and chief of the infantry and cavalry of Gaoyang Gate; was transferred to commander of all four companies of the Celestial Martial and Sun-Rising guards; and was again transferred to vice commander of the infantry army, defense commissioner of Meizhou, and deputy chief general of the Bingdai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commander of all four companies of the Dragon Spirit Guard, regimented trainer of Zhongzhou, and chief of the infantry and cavalry of Gaoyang Gate; was transferred to commander of all four companies of the Celestial Martial and Sun-Rising guards; and was again made vice commander of the infantry army, defense commissioner of Meizhou, and deputy chief general of the Bingdai circuit.

sentences.zh: 判北京賈昌朝奏為大名府路副都總管，徙定州路，遷馬軍都虞候，徙鄜延路，行至鄭州卒，贈遂州觀察使。

translations.literal: The Court delegate of the Northern Capital Jia Changchao memorialized to appoint him deputy chief general of the Daming Prefecture circuit; he was transferred to the Dingzhou circuit, was promoted to vice commander of the cavalry army, was transferred to the Zhenyan circuit, and died at Zhengzhou on the way; he was posthumously awarded observation commissioner of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Court delegate of the Northern Capital Jia Changchao recommended him as deputy chief general of the Daming Prefecture circuit; he was transferred to the Dingzhou circuit, promoted to vice commander of the cavalry army, and moved to the Zhenyan circuit, but died at Zhengzhou en route and was posthumously awarded observation commissioner of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 劉謙，字漢宗，開封人。

translations.literal: Liu Qian, styled Hanzong, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qian, styled Hanzong, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少補衛士，數遷至捧日右廂都指揮使，領嘉州團練使兼京城巡檢。

translations.literal: In youth he was supplementary palace guard; through several promotions he reached commander of the right company of the Sun-Rising Guard, holding the post of regimented trainer of Jiazhou while also serving as capital circuit inspector.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he entered the palace guard corps and, through several promotions, rose to commander of the right company of the Sun-Rising Guard, serving as regimented trainer of Jiazhou while also acting as capital circuit inspector.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，改博州團練使、環慶路馬步軍總管兼知邠州。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao rebelled, he was changed to regimented trainer of Bozhou, chief of infantry and cavalry of the Huanqing circuit, and concurrent prefect of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao rebelled, he was reassigned as regimented trainer of Bozhou, chief of infantry and cavalry of the Huanqing circuit, and concurrent prefect of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 謙不讀書，然鬥訟曲直，皆區處當理。

translations.literal: Qian did not read books, yet in disputes and lawsuits over right and wrong he adjudicated everything properly.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was not a reader, yet in disputes and lawsuits he judged every case fairly and soundly.

sentences.zh: 前守者多強市民物以飾廚傳，謙獨無所撓，邠人頗愛之。

translations.literal: Previous prefects mostly forcibly bought goods from townspeople to adorn their official kitchens and guest quarters; Qian alone did nothing of the sort, and the people of Bin greatly liked him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier prefects had often forcibly bought goods from townspeople to furnish their kitchens and guest quarters, but Qian never did so, and the people of Bin came to love him.

sentences.zh: 夏竦奏為涇原路總管，徙知涇州，未行，會賊寇鎮戎軍，謙引兵深入賊境，破其聚落而還。

translations.literal: Xia Song memorialized to appoint him chief general of the Jingyuan circuit; he was transferred to serve as prefect of Jingzhou; before he set out, bandits raided Zhenrong Army; Qian led troops deep into enemy territory, destroyed their settlements, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song recommended him as chief general of the Jingyuan circuit and transferred him to serve as prefect of Jingzhou; before he departed, bandits raided Zhenrong Army, and Qian led troops deep into enemy territory, destroyed their settlements, and returned.

sentences.zh: 以功擢龍神衛四廂都指揮使、象州防禦使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to commander of all four companies of the Dragon Spirit Guard and defense commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to commander of all four companies of the Dragon Spirit Guard and defense commissioner of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 暴疾卒，贈永清軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: He died suddenly of illness and was posthumously awarded military governor and observation commissioner of Yongqing Army, remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly of illness and was posthumously awarded military governor and observation commissioner of Yongqing Army, remaining in office.

sentences.zh: 趙振，字仲威，雄州歸信人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhen, styled Zhongwei, was a native of Guixin in Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhen, styled Zhongwei, came from Guixin in Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德中，從石普於順安軍。

translations.literal: During the Jingde era he followed Shi Pu at Shun'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era he served under Shi Pu at Shun'an Army.

sentences.zh: 獲契丹陣圖，授三班借職。

translations.literal: He captured a Khitan battle formation map and was awarded third-class borrowed office.
translations.idiomatic: He captured a Khitan battle formation map and was granted third-class borrowed office.

sentences.zh: 後數年，為隰州兵馬監押，捕盜於青灰山，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Several years later he served as military supervisor of Xi Prefecture; at Qinghui Mountain he captured bandits, killing and capturing very many.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, as military supervisor of Xi Prefecture, he hunted bandits at Qinghui Mountain and killed or captured a great many of them.

sentences.zh: 高平蠻叛，徙湖北都巡檢使兼制置南路。

translations.literal: When the Gaoping barbarians rebelled, he was transferred to chief circuit inspector of Hubei and concurrently assigned to manage the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaoping barbarians rebelled, he was transferred to chief circuit inspector of Hubei and concurrently put in charge of the southern route.

sentences.zh: 以南方暑濕，弓弩不利，別創小矢，激三百步，中輒洞穿，蠻遂駭散。

translations.literal: Because the southern region was hot and humid and crossbows were ineffective, he specially created small arrows that could be shot three hundred paces; when they hit they pierced through; the barbarians were thus terrified and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Because the southern heat and humidity made crossbows ineffective, he devised small arrows that could be shot three hundred paces and pierced clean through on impact; the barbarians were terrified and scattered.

sentences.zh: 歲中，遷慶州沿邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Within the year he was transferred to chief border inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was transferred to chief border inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時，金湯李欽、白豹神木馬兒、高羅跛臧三族尤悍難制，振募降羌，啖以利，令相攻，破十餘堡。

translations.literal: At the time the three tribes of Jintang Li Qin, Baimu Shenma'er, and Gaoluo Bozang were especially fierce and hard to control; Zhen recruited surrendered Qiang, enticed them with profit, and had them attack one another, destroying more than ten forts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the three tribes of Jintang Li Qin, Baimu Shenma'er, and Gaoluo Bozang were especially fierce and hard to control; Zhen recruited surrendered Qiang, tempted them with rewards, and set them against one another, destroying more than ten forts.

sentences.zh: 欽等詣振自歸。

translations.literal: Qin and the others came to Zhen and surrendered of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and the others came to Zhen and surrendered of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 振為置酒，先釂，取細仗，圍財數分，植百步外共射。

translations.literal: Zhen set out wine for them; he drank first, took fine weapons, divided the spoils into several piles, set them a hundred paces away, and they all shot at them together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen set out wine for them, drank first himself, took fine weapons, divided the spoils into several piles, placed them a hundred paces away, and had them all shoot together.

sentences.zh: 欽等百發不中，振十矢皆貫，欽等皆驚，誓不復敢犯。

translations.literal: Qin and the others shot a hundred times without hitting; Zhen's ten arrows all passed through; Qin and the others were all astonished and swore never again to dare to violate.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and the others fired a hundred shots without hitting once; Zhen's ten arrows all passed clean through; they were all astonished and swore never again to dare attack him.

sentences.zh: 明年，涇原屬羌胡薩逋歌等叛，鈐轄王懷信以兵數千屬振遊奕，屢捷。

translations.literal: The next year Hu Saboge of the affiliated Qiang of Jingyuan and others rebelled; Deputy Military Commissioner Wang Huaixin placed several thousand troops under Zhen for roving patrol; he repeatedly won victories.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Hu Saboge of the affiliated Qiang of Jingyuan and others rebelled; Deputy Military Commissioner Wang Huaixin assigned several thousand troops to Zhen for roving patrol, and he won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 從數十騎詣懷信，遇賊十倍，射殪數十，餘悉退散。

translations.literal: With several dozen horsemen he went to see Huaixin; he encountered bandits ten times their number, shot and killed several dozen, and the rest all retreated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Riding with several dozen men to see Huaixin, he encountered bandits ten times their number, shot and killed several dozen, and put the rest to flight.

sentences.zh: 數月，賊數萬圍平遠砦，都監趙士龍戰沒。

translations.literal: Several months later, several tens of thousands of bandits besieged Pingyuan Stockade; Supervisor Zhao Shilong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, several tens of thousands of bandits besieged Pingyuan Stockade, and Supervisor Zhao Shilong was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 振出別道，力戰抵砦，奪取水泉，率敢死士破圍，賊走，追斬數千級，徙涇原都鹽，歷知順安、保安、廣信軍、霸州，改京東都大提舉捉賊。

translations.literal: Zhen took another route, fought fiercely to reach the stockade, seized water sources, led dare-to-die soldiers to break the siege, the bandits fled, he pursued and beheaded several thousand; he was transferred to chief salt commissioner of Jingyuan, successively served as prefect of Shun'an, Bao'an, and Guangxin armies and Bazhou, and was changed to chief commissioner for capturing bandits in the eastern capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen took another route, fought his way to the stockade, seized its water supply, and led dare-to-die troops to break the siege; the bandits fled, and he pursued and beheaded several thousand. He was transferred to chief salt commissioner of Jingyuan, served successively as prefect of Shun'an, Bao'an, and Guangxin armies and of Bazhou, and was then made chief commissioner for capturing bandits in the eastern capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 明年，知環州，累遷象州防禦使。

translations.literal: The next year he served as prefect of Huanzhou and was promoted in succession to defense commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he served as prefect of Huanzhou and was promoted in succession to defense commissioner of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 元昊將反，為金銀冠珮隱飾甲騎遺屬羌，振潛以金帛誘取之，以破其勢，得冠珮銀鞍三千、甲騎數百。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao was about to rebel, he gave gold and silver crowns and pendants and secretly adorned cavalry armor as gifts to the affiliated Qiang; Zhen secretly used gold and silk to lure and take them back, thereby breaking their strength; he obtained three thousand crowns, pendants, and silver saddles and several hundred armored horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao was about to rebel, he sent gold and silver crowns and pendants and secretly adorned cavalry armor as gifts to the affiliated Qiang; Zhen secretly lured them back with gold and silk, breaking their strength and recovering three thousand crowns, pendants, and silver saddles along with several hundred armored horsemen.

sentences.zh: 告鄰部俾以環為法，不聽，於是東茭、金明、萬劉諸族勝兵數萬，悉為賊所有。

translations.literal: He told neighboring prefectures to take Huan as their model, but they would not listen; thereupon the tribes of Dongjiao, Jinming, Wanliu and others — several tens of thousands of able soldiers — all came into the possession of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He urged neighboring prefectures to follow Huan's example, but they would not listen; as a result, the tribes of Dongjiao, Jinming, Wanliu, and others — several tens of thousands of able fighters — all fell into enemy hands.

sentences.zh: 及劉平等皆敗，唯環慶無患。

translations.literal: When Liu Ping and others were all defeated, only Huanqing was without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ping and the others were all defeated, Huanqing alone remained untroubled.

sentences.zh: 自本路馬步軍副總管擢龍神衛四廂都指揮使、鄜延路副都總管、知延州，代范雍。

translations.literal: From deputy chief general of infantry and cavalry of this circuit he was promoted to commander of all four companies of the Dragon Spirit Guard, deputy chief general of the Zhenyan circuit, and prefect of Yanzhou, replacing Fan Yong.
translations.idiomatic: From deputy chief general of infantry and cavalry of his circuit he was promoted to commander of all four companies of the Dragon Spirit Guard, deputy chief general of the Zhenyan circuit, and prefect of Yanzhou, replacing Fan Yong.

sentences.zh: 尋改捧日、天武四廂。

translations.literal: Soon after he was changed to the four companies of the Sun-Rising and Celestial Martial guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was transferred to the four companies of the Sun-Rising and Celestial Martial guards.

sentences.zh: 振謂將吏曰：「今賊以我夷傷，必乘勝以進，勢宜固守。

translations.literal: Zhen said to the officers and clerks: "Now the enemy, because we have suffered heavy casualties, is sure to press forward on the momentum of victory; the situation calls for firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen told his officers and clerks, "The enemy, seeing that we have suffered heavy casualties, is sure to press forward on the momentum of victory; the wise course is to stand firm and defend.

sentences.zh: 尚慮諸城不能皆如吾謀，苟延州弗支，則陝西未可測，此天下安危之機也。」

translations.literal: I still fear that not every city can follow our plan; if Yanzhou cannot hold, then Shaanxi west of the mountains cannot be foreseen — this is the hinge of the empire's safety and peril."
translations.idiomatic: I still worry that not every city can follow our plan; if Yanzhou cannot hold, then the fate of Shaanxi west of the mountains is impossible to predict — this is the hinge on which the empire's safety turns."

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊寇塞門砦。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy raided Saimen Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy raided Saimen Stockade.

sentences.zh: 振有兵幾八千，按甲不動。

translations.literal: Zhen had nearly eight thousand troops but kept his armor on and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had nearly eight thousand troops but kept his armor on and did not move.

sentences.zh: 砦中兵才千人，屢告急，被圍五月，才遣百餘人赴之，砦遂陷。

translations.literal: The stockade had only a thousand troops; they repeatedly sent urgent appeals; besieged for five months, he sent only a little over a hundred men to their aid, and the stockade then fell.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade had only a thousand men and sent repeated urgent appeals; after five months under siege, Zhen sent only a little over a hundred men to their aid, and the stockade fell.

sentences.zh: 砦主高延德、鹽押王繼元皆沒於賊。

translations.literal: Stockade commander Gao Yande and salt supervisor Wang Jiyuan both perished at the hands of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Stockade commander Gao Yande and salt supervisor Wang Jiyuan both fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 振坐擁兵不救，為都轉運使龐籍所奏，貶白州團練使、知絳州。

translations.literal: Zhen was punished for holding troops and not rescuing them; Circuit Transport Commissioner Pang Ji memorialized against him, and he was demoted to regimented trainer of Baizhou and prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was punished for holding troops and failing to rescue the stockade; Circuit Transport Commissioner Pang Ji memorialized against him, and he was demoted to regimented trainer of Baizhou and prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，會延德、繼元家復訴於朝，敕御史方偕就劾振。

translations.literal: Before he set out, the families of Yande and Jiyuan again appealed at court; the emperor ordered Censor Fang Xie to go and impeach Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, the families of Yande and Jiyuan appealed again at court, and the emperor ordered Censor Fang Xie to go and impeach Zhen.

sentences.zh: 法當斬，再貶太子左清道率府率、潭州安置。

translations.literal: By law he should have been executed; he was demoted again to colonel of the Left Clear Way Escort of the Heir Apparent's Household and assigned to Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By law he deserved execution; he was demoted again to colonel of the Left Clear Way Escort of the Heir Apparent's Household and assigned to Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復右武衛將軍、惠州團練使、幷代路兵馬鈐轄，就遷副總管、祁州團練使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was restored to Right Martial Guard general, regimented trainer of Huizhou, and deputy military commissioner of the Bingdai circuit, and was immediately transferred to deputy chief general and regimented trainer of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was restored as Right Martial Guard general, regimented trainer of Huizhou, and deputy military commissioner of the Bingdai circuit, and was immediately promoted to deputy chief general and regimented trainer of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 元昊既破豐州，將襲近砦，振率鈐轄張亢、麥允言出麟州深柏堰，擊破之。

translations.literal: After Yuanhao had taken Fengzhou and was about to raid nearby stockades, Zhen led Deputy Military Commissioners Zhang Kang and Mai Yunyan out from Shenbai Weir of Lin Prefecture and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanhao captured Fengzhou and was about to raid nearby stockades, Zhen led Deputy Military Commissioners Zhang Kang and Mai Yunyan out from Shenbai Weir of Lin Prefecture and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 兼領嵐、憲六州軍事。

translations.literal: He concurrently held military affairs of the six prefectures and armies of Lan and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He also took charge of military affairs in the six prefectures and armies of Lan and Xian.

sentences.zh: 河外饑，振設法通砦外商，得米數十萬斛，軍民以濟。

translations.literal: When the region beyond the Yellow River suffered famine, Zhen devised a method to open trade with merchants outside the stockades and obtained several hundred thousand bushels of rice; army and people were thereby saved.
translations.idiomatic: When the region beyond the Yellow River suffered famine, Zhen devised a way to open trade with merchants outside the stockades and obtained several hundred thousand bushels of rice, saving both army and people.

sentences.zh: 進博州防禦使，改解州致仕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to defense commissioner of Bozhou and changed to retired status at Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to defense commissioner of Bozhou and then retired at Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 復起為左神武軍大將軍，卒。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as great general of the Left Divine Martial Army and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as great general of the Left Divine Martial Army and died in office.

sentences.zh: 振剛強自負，有武力，便弓馬，喜謀畫，輕財尚氣，眾樂為用。

translations.literal: Zhen was strong-willed and self-confident, possessed martial prowess, was skilled with bow and horse, liked planning, held wealth lightly and valued honor, and the masses were glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was strong-willed and proud, skilled in arms and adept with bow and horse, fond of strategy, generous and high-spirited, and men were glad to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 子珣、瑜，皆工騎射。

translations.literal: His sons Xun and Yu were both skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xun and Yu were both skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 珣年十六，仁宗召試便殿，授三班借職。

translations.literal: At age sixteen Xun was summoned by Emperor Renzong to be tested in the Informal Hall and was awarded third-class borrowed office.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, Xun was summoned by Emperor Renzong to demonstrate his skills in the Informal Hall and was granted third-class borrowed office.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，有言珣藝益進，且習書史。

translations.literal: During Jingyou it was reported that Xun's skill had advanced further and that he was also studying books and history.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyou era it was reported that Xun's skills had improved further and that he was also studying books and history.

sentences.zh: 復召見閱武伎，又試策略於中書，條對數千言。

translations.literal: He was again summoned and his martial skills were reviewed; he was also tested on strategy at the Secretariat and responded item by item in several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again to demonstrate his martial skills and was also tested on strategy at the Secretariat, where he answered at length in several thousand words.

sentences.zh: 自殿直進閤門祗候，未幾，除濠州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: From palace attendant he was promoted to gatekeeper attendant of the Inner Gate, and before long was appointed military superintendent of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from palace attendant to gatekeeper attendant of the Inner Gate, and before long was appointed military superintendent of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，珣隨父在西邊，訪得五路徼外形勝利害，作《聚米圖經》五卷。

translations.literal: At first Xun followed his father on the western frontier, investigated the strategic advantages and disadvantages along the borders of the five circuits, and composed the five-scroll Gathered-Rice Atlas.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Xun had followed his father on the western frontier, investigated the strategic terrain along the borders of the five circuits, and composed the five-scroll Gathered-Rice Atlas.

sentences.zh: 詔取其書，並召珣至，又上《五陣圖》、《兵事》十餘篇。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his book taken and Xun summoned as well; he also submitted more than ten chapters on the Five Formations Diagram and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered his book brought in and summoned Xun as well; he also submitted more than ten chapters on the Five Formations Diagram and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝給步騎使按陣，既成，臨觀之。

translations.literal: The emperor supplied infantry and cavalry for him to arrange formations; when it was done, he watched in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor supplied infantry and cavalry for him to drill in formation, and when the drill was complete, watched in person.

sentences.zh: 陳執中招討陝西，薦為緣邊巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Chen Zhizhong was appointed pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, he recommended Xun as border circuit inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zhizhong was appointed pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, he recommended Xun as border circuit inspector.

sentences.zh: 呂夷簡、宋庠為奏曰：「用兵以來，策士之言以萬計，無如珣者。

translations.literal: Lü Yijian and Song Qi memorialized on his behalf, saying: "Since the use of troops began, the words of strategists have numbered in the tens of thousands, yet none have matched Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yijian and Song Qi memorialized on his behalf, saying, "Since the war began, strategists have submitted tens of thousands of proposals, yet none have matched Xun.

sentences.zh: 」即擢通事舍人、招討都監。

translations.literal: " He was immediately promoted to Protocol Envoy and pacification chief supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: " He was immediately promoted to Protocol Envoy and pacification chief supervisor.

sentences.zh: 珣自以年少新進，辭都監。

translations.literal: Xun, considering himself young and newly advanced, declined the chief supervisor post.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, considering himself young and newly advanced, declined the chief supervisor post.

sentences.zh: 授兵萬人，御賜鎧仗，令自擇偏裨、參佐，居涇原，兼治籠竿城。

translations.literal: He was given ten thousand troops, armor and weapons bestowed by the emperor, and ordered to choose his own subordinate commanders and staff; he resided in Jingyuan and concurrently administered Longgan City.
translations.idiomatic: He was given ten thousand troops and imperial armor and weapons, and was allowed to choose his own subordinate commanders and staff; he was stationed in Jingyuan and also administered Longgan City.

sentences.zh: 麻氈、黨留百餘帳處近塞為暴，珣白府，引兵二萬，自靜邊歷揆吳抵木寧襲賊，俘獲數千計。

translations.literal: More than a hundred tents of Ma Zhan and Dang Liu near the border committed violence; Xun reported to headquarters, led twenty thousand troops from Jingbian through Kuiwu to Muning to raid the bandits, and captured several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred tents of Ma Zhan and Dang Liu near the border were raiding and plundering; Xun reported to headquarters, led twenty thousand troops from Jingbian through Kuiwu to Muning to strike the bandits, and captured several thousand.

sentences.zh: 靜邊將劉滬殿後，為賊所掩。

translations.literal: Jingbian commander Liu Hu brought up the rear and was ambushed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbian commander Liu Hu brought up the rear and was ambushed by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 珣登阪望見，從騎數百復入，拔滬之眾以出，士皆歎服。

translations.literal: Xun climbed a slope and saw it; with several hundred followers he went back in, extricated Hu's force, and the soldiers all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Xun climbed a slope and saw what had happened; with several hundred followers he rode back in, rescued Hu's men, and the soldiers all marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 瞎氈居龕穀無所屬，珣與書招之，遺以綈綿，瞎氈聽命。

translations.literal: Xia Zhan lived in Kan Valley under no authority; Xun wrote to summon him, sent silk and cotton as gifts, and Xia Zhan obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Zhan lived in Kan Valley under no master; Xun wrote to summon him, sent gifts of silk and cotton, and Xia Zhan submitted.

sentences.zh: 改本路都監，詔追入朝。

translations.literal: He was changed to chief supervisor of this circuit; an edict ordered him recalled to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief supervisor of his circuit, and an edict ordered him recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 將行，適元昊大入，府檄留珣，會葛懷敏於瓦亭。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Yuanhao launched a major invasion; headquarters issued an order retaining Xun, and he joined Ge Huaimin at Wating.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to leave, Yuanhao launched a major invasion; headquarters ordered Xun to remain, and he joined Ge Huaimin at Wating.

sentences.zh: 懷敏已屯五谷口西至馬欄城，聞夏人徙軍新壕外，議欲質明掩襲。

translations.literal: Huaimin had already encamped from Wugu Pass west to Malan City; hearing that the Tangut army had moved outside the new moat, he discussed making a dawn surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin had already encamped from Wugu Pass west to Malan City; hearing that the Tangut army had moved outside the new moat, he proposed a dawn surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 珣謂懷敏曰：「敵遠來，眾倍鋒銳，莫若依馬欄城布柵以扼其路，守鎮戎城以便餉道，俟其衰擊之，此必勝之道也。

translations.literal: Xun said to Huaimin: "The enemy has come from afar, their numbers are doubled and their edge is sharp; better to rely on Malan City and set up palisades to choke their route, hold Zhenrong City to secure the supply road, wait until they weaken and then strike — this is the sure way to victory.
translations.idiomatic: Xun told Huaimin, "The enemy has marched from far away; their numbers are doubled and their edge is sharp. Better to fortify Malan City with palisades to block their route, hold Zhenrong City to secure the supply line, and wait until they weaken before striking — that is the sure path to victory.

sentences.zh: 不然，必為賊所屠。

translations.literal: Otherwise you will surely be slaughtered by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you will surely be slaughtered by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」懷敏不聽，兵遂逼鎮戎城，越界壕，抵定川。

translations.literal: " Huaimin would not listen; the army then pressed on Zhenrong City, crossed the border moat, and reached Dingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: " Huaimin would not listen; the army pressed on to Zhenrong City, crossed the border moat, and reached Dingchuan.

sentences.zh: 未及陣，夏人引鐵騎來犯，珣居陣西北，瑜亦在軍中，戰甚力。

translations.literal: Before they could form ranks, the Tangut led iron cavalry to attack; Xun was on the northwest of the formation, Yu was also in the army, and they fought very fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could form ranks, the Tangut led iron cavalry against them; Xun held the northwest of the formation, Yu was also in the army, and both fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 東壁兵輒潰，中軍大擾，珣擁刀斧手前鬥，夏眾稍卻，我軍復陣。

translations.literal: The troops on the eastern wall suddenly collapsed; the central army was greatly thrown into disorder; Xun led axemen forward to fight; the Tangut masses retreated slightly, and our army re-formed.
translations.idiomatic: The troops on the eastern flank suddenly broke; the center was thrown into chaos; Xun led his axemen forward to fight, the Tangut lines fell back slightly, and the army re-formed.

sentences.zh: 懷敏詰朝退走，就食鎮戎。

translations.literal: Huaimin withdrew at dawn the next day and went to take provisions at Zhenrong.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day Huaimin withdrew and went to Zhenrong for provisions.

sentences.zh: 俄夏騎四合，珣被擒，瑜以身免。

translations.literal: Soon Tangut horsemen closed in from all sides; Xun was captured, and Yu escaped by himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tangut horsemen closed in from all sides; Xun was captured, and Yu escaped alone.

sentences.zh: 珣美風儀，性勁特好學，恂恂類儒者。

translations.literal: Xun had fine bearing, was by nature firm and special and fond of learning, and was modest and respectful like a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had a fine bearing, was resolute and studious by nature, and carried himself with the modest courtesy of a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 既沒，人多惜之。

translations.literal: After his death many people regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: After his death many mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 贈莫州刺史，後卒賊中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded prefect of Mo Prefecture; later he died among the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded prefect of Mo Prefecture and later died in enemy hands.

sentences.zh: 瑜弟璞，亦知名。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Pu was also well known.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Pu was also well known.

sentences.zh: 范恪，字許國，開封人。

translations.literal: Fan Ke, styled Xuguo, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ke, styled Xuguo, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初名全，少隸軍籍於許州，選入捧日軍，又選為殿前指揮使，歷行門、龍旗直、散員押班。

translations.literal: His original name was Quan; in youth he entered army rolls at Xuzhou, was selected into the Sun-Rising Army, was again selected as commander of the Palace Front, and successively served in the Procession Gate, Dragon Banner, and scattered company escort posts.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Quan; as a youth he entered the army rolls at Xuzhou, was selected into the Sun-Rising Army, and later chosen as commander of the Palace Front, serving successively in the Procession Gate, Dragon Banner, and scattered company escort posts.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，元昊數寇邊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, Yuanhao repeatedly raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangding, Yuanhao repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 試武伎，擢內殿崇班、慶州北路都巡檢使，與攻白豹城，破之。

translations.literal: His martial skills were tested; he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Company and chief northern-route circuit inspector of Qingzhou; he joined the attack on Baibao City and took it.
translations.idiomatic: After his martial skills were tested, he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Company and chief northern-route circuit inspector of Qingzhou; he joined the attack on Baibao City and captured it.

sentences.zh: 既還，夏人遣騎襲其後。

translations.literal: Having returned, the Xia people sent horsemen to attack from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, the Tangut sent cavalry to strike from the rear.

sentences.zh: 恪設伏崖險，敵半度，邀擊之，斬首四百級，生獲七十餘人。

translations.literal: Ke set an ambush on a perilous cliff; when the enemy was half across, he intercepted and struck them, beheading four hundred and capturing alive more than seventy men.
translations.idiomatic: Ke laid an ambush on a treacherous cliff pass; when the enemy was halfway across, he intercepted them, taking four hundred heads and more than seventy prisoners.

sentences.zh: 以功遷內殿承制。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Inner Hall Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to Inner Hall Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘗會諸道兵攻十二盤暨咄當、迷子砦，中流矢，督戰愈力。

translations.literal: He once joined troops from the various circuits to attack Shierpan as well as the Zhuodang and Mizi forts; struck by an arrow mid-stream, he pressed the battle all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: He once combined forces from several circuits to attack Shierpan and the Zhuodang and Mizi forts; though struck by an arrow in the fighting, he directed the battle with even greater force.

sentences.zh: 視炮石中有火爨者，恪取號於眾曰：「賊矢石盡，用灶下甓矣。

translations.literal: Seeing fire for cooking among the catapult stones, Ke shouted to the host, saying: "The bandits' arrows and stones are exhausted—they are using bricks from beneath the stove.
translations.idiomatic: Noticing cooking fires among the stones hurled by catapults, Ke cried out to the troops: "The enemy has run out of arrows and stones—they are throwing bricks from under their stoves!

sentences.zh: 」於是士卒爭奮，果先得城。

translations.literal: " At this the soldiers competed in ardor, and indeed took the city first.
translations.idiomatic: At that the soldiers surged forward with fresh zeal and were indeed the first to take the city.

sentences.zh: 遷供備庫副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Provision and Equipment Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Provision and Equipment Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 恪有弓勝一石七斗，其箭鏃如鏵，名曰鏵弓。

translations.literal: Ke had a bow exceeding one picul and seven pecks in strength; its arrowheads were like plowshares, and it was called the Plowshare Bow.
translations.idiomatic: Ke owned a bow with a draw weight of more than one picul and seven pecks; its arrowheads were shaped like plowshares, and the weapon was known as the Plowshare Bow.

sentences.zh: 又於羽間識其官稱、姓氏，凡所發必中，至一箭貫二人。

translations.literal: He also marked rank titles and surnames between the fletchings; every shot he loosed hit true, and on one occasion a single arrow pierced two men.
translations.idiomatic: He also inscribed rank titles and surnames between the fletchings; every arrow he released found its mark, and once a single shaft pierced two men.

sentences.zh: 他日，取蕉蒿砦歸，恪獨殿後，為數千騎所襲。

translations.literal: Another day, on returning from taking Jiaohao Fort, Ke alone brought up the rear and was attacked by several thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, after capturing Jiaohao Fort on the return march, Ke alone held the rear and was set upon by several thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 屬視矢箙止有二鏵，即為引滿之勢，賊遽卻。

translations.literal: Just then he saw only two plowshare arrows left in his quiver; he at once drew to the full, and the bandits immediately withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Glancing back, he saw only two plowshare arrows left in his quiver; he at once drew the bow to the full, and the enemy fled at once.

sentences.zh: 嘗與總管杜惟序、鈐轄高繼隆將兵分討漢乞、薛馬、都嵬等三砦，恪先破都嵬，而繼隆圍薛馬不能下，恪馳往取之，既又援惟序下漢乞砦。

translations.literal: He once joined Chief Commander Du Weixu and Commandant Gao Jilong in leading troops to attack separately the three forts of Hanqi, Xuema, and Douwei; Ke first broke Douwei, while Jilong besieged Xuema but could not take it—Ke galloped there and captured it, then went again to relieve Weixu and take Hanqi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He once joined Chief Commander Du Weixu and Commandant Gao Jilong in dividing forces to subdue the three forts of Hanqi, Xuema, and Douwei. Ke first broke Douwei; Jilong besieged Xuema but could not reduce it, so Ke galloped to take it himself, then turned back to relieve Weixu and capture Hanqi Fort.

sentences.zh: 改左騏驥副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Deputy Commander of the Left Qilin Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Deputy Commander of the Left Qilin Guard.

sentences.zh: 虜犯大順城，諸將皆閉城自守。

translations.literal: The barbarians attacked Dashun City, and all the generals closed the gates and held themselves within.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy attacked Dashun City, every general shut the gates and held fast within the walls.

sentences.zh: 恪率兵二千餘，戰克之。

translations.literal: Ke led a little over two thousand men and fought to victory.
translations.idiomatic: Ke led a little more than two thousand men and fought them to victory.

sentences.zh: 改宮苑副使、環慶路兵馬都監，因特召見。

translations.literal: He was made Deputy Commissioner of the Palace Parks and Chief Military Inspector of Huanqing Circuit, and was specially summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Palace Parks and Chief Military Inspector of Huanqing Circuit, and was specially summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 仁宗謂曰：「適有邊奏，賊犯高平軍劉璠堡，可乘驛亟往。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said to him: "There has just come a frontier report that bandits have attacked Liu Fan's fort at Gaoping Army—you may take the courier route and go at once.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong said to him, "A frontier report has just arrived: bandits are attacking Liu Fan's fort at Gaoping Army. Take the courier route and go at once.

sentences.zh: 」遂遷禮賓使、榮州刺史、環慶路鈐轄，手詔令趣范仲淹麾下起兵赴援。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon promoted to Commissioner of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests, Prefect of Rongzhou, and Commandant of Huanqing Circuit; an imperial handwritten edict ordered him to hasten under Fan Zhongyan's command to raise troops for relief.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon promoted to Commissioner of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests, Prefect of Rongzhou, and Commandant of Huanqing Circuit, and an imperial handwritten edict ordered him to hurry to Fan Zhongyan's command and raise troops for relief.

sentences.zh: 恪晝夜兼行，比至平涼，賊已解。

translations.literal: Ke traveled day and night without pause; by the time he reached Pingliang, the bandits had already dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Ke pressed on day and night without rest, but by the time he reached Pingliang the enemy had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷洛苑使，權秦鳳路兵馬總管。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he was promoted to Commissioner of the Luoyang Park and acting Chief Military Commander of Qinfeng Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Commissioner of the Luoyang Park and acting Chief Military Commander of Qinfeng Circuit.

sentences.zh: 恪驍勇善射，臨難敢前，故數有戰功，自龍、神衛四廂都指揮使累遷至侍衛親軍馬步軍副都指揮使，曆坊州刺史、解州防禦、宣州觀察使、保信軍節度觀察留後，以疾出為永興軍路副都總管，數月卒，贈昭化軍節度使。

translations.literal: Ke was fierce and brave and skilled in archery; facing peril he dared advance—hence he repeatedly won battle merit. From Commandant of the Four Wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard he rose in succession to Deputy Chief Commander of the Palace Guard's horse and foot armies, and served as Prefect of Fangzhou, Defender of Jiezhou, Observer of Xuanzhou, and Acting Military Commissioner and Observer of the Baoxin Army; due to illness he was sent out as Deputy Chief Commander of the Yongxing Army Route and died within several months; posthumously enfeoffed as Military Commissioner of the Zhaohua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was fierce, brave, and a fine archer who dared press forward in danger, and so he won battle honors again and again. From commandant of the four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard he rose in succession to deputy chief commander of the Palace Guard's horse and foot armies, serving as prefect of Fangzhou, defender of Jiezhou, observer of Xuanzhou, and acting military commissioner and observer of the Baoxin Army. Illness sent him out as deputy chief commander of the Yongxing Army Route; he died within a few months and was posthumously enfeoffed as military commissioner of the Zhaohua Army.

sentences.zh: 馬懷德

translations.literal: Ma Huaide
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huaide

sentences.zh: 馬懷德，字得之，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Ma Huaide, styled Dezhi, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huaide, styled Dezhi, came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父玉，東頭供奉官，言懷德可試引弓、擊劍、角觝，補三班奉職，為延州南安砦主、東路巡檢。
