translations.literal: His father Yu was an Eastern Head Palace Attendant; he said Huaide could be tested in bow-drawing, swordsmanship, and wrestling, and he was appointed Third-Rank Palace Attendant, serving as master of Nan'an Fort at Yanzhou and eastern-route inspector.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was an Eastern Head Palace Attendant; he reported that Huaide could be tested in archery, swordplay, and wrestling, and Huaide was appointed Third-Rank Palace Attendant, serving as master of Nan'an Fort at Yanzhou and eastern-route inspector.

sentences.zh: 數以少擊西賊，敗其眾。

translations.literal: Several times with few men he struck the Western bandits and routed their hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Several times he attacked the Western bandits with small forces and routed their armies.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹知延州，修青澗城，奏懷德為兵馬監押，以所部兵入賊境，破遮鹿、要冊二砦，親射殺其酋狗兒廂主，遷左班殿直。

translations.literal: When Fan Zhongyan governed Yanzhou and built Qingjian City, he memorialized for Huaide as military supervisor; with the troops under his command he entered bandit territory and broke the Zhelu and Yaoche forts, personally shooting dead their chieftain Gou'erxiangzhu; he was promoted to Left Hall Gentlemen of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan governed Yanzhou and built Qingjian City, he recommended Huaide as military supervisor. Leading his own troops into enemy territory, Huaide broke the Zhelu and Yaoche forts and personally shot dead their chieftain Gou'erxiangzhu; he was promoted to Left Hall Gentlemen of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 又率蕃漢燒蕩賊海溝、茶山、龍柏、安化十七砦三百餘帳，斬首數百級，虜馬駝牛羊萬數，遷右侍禁。

translations.literal: He also led Tangut and Han forces to burn and scour seventeen forts—Haigou, Chashan, Longbai, and Anhua—over three hundred tents, beheading several hundred, and capturing enemy horses, camels, cattle, and sheep by the tens of thousands; he was promoted to Right Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also led Tangut and Han troops to burn and scour seventeen forts at Haigou, Chashan, Longbai, and Anhua—more than three hundred tents in all—taking several hundred heads and tens of thousands of enemy horses, camels, cattle, and sheep; he was promoted to Right Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 以范仲淹、韓琦薦，授閣門祗候，延州龐籍入奏為東路都巡檢使。

translations.literal: On recommendation by Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi, he was appointed Palace Gate Attendant; Pang Ji of Yanzhou entered court to report and he was made eastern-route chief inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi, he was appointed Palace Gate Attendant; Pang Ji of Yanzhou reported to court and had him made eastern-route chief inspector.

sentences.zh: 夷黑神、厥保等十八砦，賊以四萬騎犯邊，趨僕射穀。

translations.literal: At the eighteen forts of Yiheishen, Juebao, and others, bandits with forty thousand horsemen violated the border and rushed toward Pushe Valley.
translations.idiomatic: At the eighteen forts of Yiheishen, Juebao, and the rest, the enemy crossed the border with forty thousand horsemen and drove toward Pushe Valley.

sentences.zh: 懷德以兵數千據穀旁高原待之，斬首二百級，得畜產、器械以千數。

translations.literal: Huaide with several thousand men held the high ground beside the valley awaiting them, beheading two hundred and capturing livestock and weapons by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide took several thousand men to the high ground beside the valley and waited; he took two hundred heads and captured livestock and weapons by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 遷內殿崇班。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inner Hall Honored Company.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Company.

sentences.zh: 又以兵修龍安城，虜不敢犯，遂為鄜延路都監。

translations.literal: He again used troops to repair Long'an City; the barbarians did not dare violate it, and he then became circuit inspector of Fuyan Route.
translations.idiomatic: He again used troops to repair Long'an City; the enemy did not dare attack, and he was then made circuit inspector of Fuyan Route.

sentences.zh: 又城綏平，破賊青化、押班、吃當三砦，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: He also walled Suiping and broke the bandit forts of Qinghua, Yaban, and Chidang, killing and capturing in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He also fortified Suiping and broke the enemy forts of Qinghua, Yaban, and Chidang, killing and capturing a great many of the foe.

sentences.zh: 元昊為夏國主，命國子博士高良夫與懷德會西人畫界。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao became ruler of the Xia state, he ordered State Academy Doctor Gao Liangfu to meet with Huaide and the Westerners to demarcate the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao became ruler of the Xia state, he ordered State Academy Doctor Gao Liangfu to meet with Huaide and the Westerners to demarcate the border.

sentences.zh: 龐籍具論其前後功，遷供備庫副使兼閣門通事舍人。

translations.literal: Pang Ji set forth his achievements before and after in full; he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Provision and Equipment Storehouse, concurrently Palace Gate Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji laid out his achievements in full detail, and he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Provision and Equipment Storehouse, concurrently Palace Gate Envoy.

sentences.zh: 時用兵久，民多亡散，懷德招輯有方，經略使梁適奏請推其法諸路。

translations.literal: Protracted warfare had scattered many of the people; Huaide had effective methods for recruiting and gathering them, and Military Commissioner Liang Shi memorialized asking that his methods be extended to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The long war had scattered many people, but Huaide had effective ways of recruiting and resettling them; Military Commissioner Liang Shi memorialized asking that his methods be applied on every circuit.

sentences.zh: 曆知保安軍、環州、環慶益利路鈐轄，累遷至四方館使、舒州團練使，徙鄜延路副都總管。

translations.literal: He successively governed Bao'an Army and Huanzhou, was Commandant of Huanqing and Yili circuits, rose in succession to Envoy of the Four Directions Hall and Regimental Commander of Shuzhou, and was transferred to Deputy Chief Commander of Fuyan Route.
translations.idiomatic: He successively governed Bao'an Army and Huanzhou, served as commandant of Huanqing and Yili circuits, rose in turn to Envoy of the Four Directions Hall and Regimental Commander of Shuzhou, and was transferred to Deputy Chief Commander of Fuyan Route.

sentences.zh: 坐違法賂宦官閻士良，為安撫呂景初奏，降四方館使、英州刺史。

translations.literal: Convicted of illegally bribing the eunuch Yan Shiliang, on memorial by Pacification Commissioner Lu Jingchu he was demoted to Envoy of the Four Directions Hall and Prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of illegally bribing the eunuch Yan Shiliang, he was demoted on memorial by Pacification Commissioner Lu Jingchu to Envoy of the Four Directions Hall and Prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大名府路總管，侍衛親軍步軍都虞候、象州防禦使、鄜延路副都總管，遷馬軍都虞候，徙環慶路。

translations.literal: Chief Commander of Daming Prefecture Route, Deputy Commander of the Palace Guard Foot Army, Defender of Xiangzhou, Deputy Chief Commander of Fuyan Route; promoted to Deputy Commander of the Horse Army and transferred to Huanqing Route.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief commander of Daming Prefecture Route, deputy commander of the Palace Guard Foot Army, defender of Xiangzhou, and deputy chief commander of Fuyan Route; he was promoted to deputy commander of the Horse Army and transferred to Huanqing Route.

sentences.zh: 環州蕃官蘇恩以其屬叛，往降之。

translations.literal: Su En, a Tangut official at Huanzhou, rebelled with his followers; Huaide went to receive his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Su En, a Tangut official at Huanzhou, rebelled with his followers, Huaide went to accept his surrender.

sentences.zh: 又遷殿前都虞候、步軍副指揮使、隨州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Deputy Commander of the Palace Front, Deputy Commander of the Foot Army, and Observer of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to deputy commander of the Palace Front, deputy commander of the Foot Army, and observer of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，遷靜難軍節度觀察留後，召還，卒，贈安遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Acting Military Commissioner and Observer of the Jingnan Army; recalled to court, he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Military Commissioner of the Anyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to acting military commissioner and observer of the Jingnan Army; recalled to court, he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as military commissioner of the Anyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 嘗因戰，流矢中其顙，鏃入於骨，以弩弦係鏃，發機而出之。

translations.literal: Once in battle a stray arrow struck his forehead and the point lodged in the bone; he tied the point with a crossbow string and pulled the trigger to draw it out.
translations.idiomatic: Once in battle a stray arrow struck his forehead and the point lodged in the bone; he tied the point to a crossbow string and pulled the trigger to draw it out.

sentences.zh: 安俊，字智周，其先太原人。

translations.literal: An Jun, styled Zhizhou; his ancestors were men of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: An Jun, styled Zhizhou, came from a Taiyuan family.

sentences.zh: 祖贇，高州團練使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun was Regimental Commander of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun was regimental commander of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇太子，俊以將家子謹厚，選為資善堂祗候。

translations.literal: When Renzong was crown prince, Jun, as the son of a military family and of careful character, was selected as attendant of the Zishan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, Jun—steady and conscientious as the son of a military family—was chosen as attendant of the Zishan Hall.

sentences.zh: 及即位，補右班殿直，累遷東頭供奉官、閣門祗候，為環州都監。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he was appointed Gentlemen of the Guard of the Right Wing, rising in succession to Eastern Head Palace Attendant and Palace Gate Attendant, and became circuit inspector of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, he was appointed Gentlemen of the Guard of the Right Wing, rose in succession to Eastern Head Palace Attendant and Palace Gate Attendant, and became circuit inspector of Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 破趙元昊吃江、井那等諸砦，安撫使韓琦上其功，遷內殿崇班、環慶路都監，徙涇原。

translations.literal: He broke the forts of Chini-jiang, Jingna, and others belonging to Zhao Yuanhao; Pacification Commissioner Han Qi reported his merit, and he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Company and circuit inspector of Huanqing Route, then transferred to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the forts of Chini-jiang, Jingna, and others held by Zhao Yuanhao; Pacification Commissioner Han Qi reported his achievements, and he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Company and circuit inspector of Huanqing Route, then transferred to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 契丹欲渝盟，與狄青、范恪同召至京師，將使備北邊，擢內園副使。

translations.literal: When the Khitans wished to violate the alliance, he was summoned to the capital together with Di Qing and Fan Ke, intending to have them prepare the northern frontier; he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Gardens.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans seemed ready to break the alliance, he was summoned to the capital together with Di Qing and Fan Ke to prepare the northern frontier; he was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Gardens.

sentences.zh: 翌日，改禮賓使。

translations.literal: The next day he was changed to Commissioner of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was reassigned as Commissioner of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests.

sentences.zh: 會葛懷敏敗，命為秦鳳路鈐轄，復徙涇原。

translations.literal: When Ge Huaimin was defeated, he was ordered to serve as Commandant of Qinfeng Route and again transferred to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Huaimin was defeated, he was ordered to serve as commandant of Qinfeng Route and was again transferred to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 因條上御戎十三事，改原州，徙麟州，遷六宅使、貴州刺史、知忻州，徙代州。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted in detail thirteen matters on frontier defense, was made Prefect of Yuanzhou, transferred to Linzhou, promoted to Commissioner of the Six Residences, Prefect of Guizhou, and Governor of Xinzhou, then transferred to Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon submitted in detail thirteen proposals on frontier defense, was made prefect of Yuanzhou, transferred to Linzhou, promoted to Commissioner of the Six Residences, prefect of Guizhou, and governor of Xinzhou, then transferred to Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 為帥臣誣奏，降京東路鈐轄。

translations.literal: Falsely impeached by a chief commander, he was demoted to Commandant of the Jingdong Route.
translations.idiomatic: Falsely impeached by a frontier commander, he was demoted to commandant of the Jingdong Route.

sentences.zh: 富弼知青州，為之辨理，真除虢州刺史，徙高陽關路，又遷原州刺史，知滄、涇、冀三州。

translations.literal: When Fu Bi governed Qingzhou he argued on his behalf; Jun was genuinely appointed Prefect of Guozhou, transferred to the Gaoyang Pass Route, again promoted to Prefect of Yuanzhou, and governed the three prefectures of Cang, Jing, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Bi governed Qingzhou he argued on his behalf; Jun was then genuinely appointed prefect of Guozhou, transferred to the Gaoyang Pass Route, again promoted to prefect of Yuanzhou, and put in charge of the three prefectures of Cang, Jing, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 秦州築古渭城，蕃部大擾，徙秦鳳路總管。

translations.literal: When Guwei City was built at Qinzhou the tribal departments were greatly disturbed; he was transferred to Chief Commander of Qinfeng Route.
translations.idiomatic: When Guwei City was built at Qinzhou and the tribal peoples were greatly disturbed, he was transferred to chief commander of Qinfeng Route.

sentences.zh: 曆龍神衛、捧日、天武四廂都指揮使，果州團練使，環慶路副總管；

translations.literal: He successively served as Commandant of the Four Wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard, Sun-Rising, and Heavenly Martial guards, Regimental Commander of Guozhou, and Deputy Chief Commander of Huanqing Route;
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as commandant of the four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard, Sun-Rising, and Heavenly Martial guards, regimental commander of Guozhou, and deputy chief commander of Huanqing Route;

sentences.zh: 遷侍衛步軍都虞候、陵州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Deputy Commander of the Palace Guard Foot Army and Defender of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Palace Guard Foot Army and defender of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈閬州觀察使。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Observer of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as observer of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 俊久在邊，羌人識之。

translations.literal: Jun had long been on the frontier; the Qiang people knew him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had long served on the frontier, and the Qiang knew him well.

sentences.zh: 環州得俘虜，知州種世衡問之曰：「若屬於吾將孰畏？

translations.literal: When Huanzhou captured prisoners, Prefect Zhong Shiheng asked them, saying: "Among our generals, whom do you fear?
translations.idiomatic: When Huanzhou took prisoners, Prefect Zhong Shiheng asked them, "Among our generals, whom do you fear?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「畏安大保。

translations.literal: " They replied: "We fear Grand Guardian An.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We fear Grand Guardian An.

sentences.zh: 」指俊於坐曰：「此長髯將軍是也。」

translations.literal: " Pointing to Jun among those seated, he said: "This long-bearded general is the man."
translations.idiomatic: Pointing to Jun among those present, he said, "This long-bearded general is the man."

sentences.zh: 向寶，鎮戎軍人，為御前忠佐，換禮賓使，涇原、秦鳳鈐轄。

translations.literal: Xiang Bao, a man of Zhenrong Army, served as a loyal aide before the throne; exchanged for Commissioner of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests, Commandant of Jingyuan and Qinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Bao, a man of Zhenrong Army, served as a loyal aide before the throne, exchanged that post for Commissioner of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests, and was commandant of Jingyuan and Qinfeng.

sentences.zh: 積勞，自皇城使帶禦器械，曆真定、鄜延副總管，遷龍神衛四廂都指揮使、嘉州團練使，卒。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit, from Commissioner of the Imperial City he carried imperial weapons; he successively served as Deputy Chief Commander of Zhending and Fuyan, was promoted to Commandant of the Four Wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard and Regimental Commander of Jiazhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he rose from Commissioner of the Imperial City with charge of imperial weapons to deputy chief commander of Zhending and Fuyan, was promoted to commandant of the four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard and regimental commander of Jiazhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 寶善騎射，年十四，與敵戰，斬首二級。

translations.literal: Bao was skilled in mounted archery; at fourteen he fought the enemy and beheaded two.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was skilled in mounted archery; at fourteen he fought the enemy and took two heads.

sentences.zh: 及壯，以勇聞。

translations.literal: When grown, he was known for his courage.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he was known for his courage.

sentences.zh: 有虎踞五原卑邪州，東西百里斷人跡，寶一矢殪之。

translations.literal: A tiger occupied Wuyuan's Beyang Prefecture and for a hundred li east and west cut off human tracks; Bao killed it with a single arrow.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger held sway over Beyang Prefecture in Wuyuan, and for a hundred li east and west no traveler dared pass; Bao brought it down with a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 道過潼關，巨盜郭邈山多載關中金帛、子女，寶射走之，盡得其所掠。

translations.literal: Passing Tong Pass, the great bandit Guo Miaoshan was carrying much gold, silk, women, and children from within the pass; Bao shot and drove him off and recovered all that had been plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Tong Pass, he found the great bandit Guo Miaoshan laden with gold, silk, women, and children plundered from within the pass; Bao shot and drove him off and recovered everything that had been taken.

sentences.zh: 嘗至太原，梁適射弩再中的，授寶矢射之，四發三中。

translations.literal: Once at Taiyuan, Liang Shi twice hit the mark shooting a crossbow; he gave Bao an arrow to shoot, and four releases hit three times.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Taiyuan, Liang Shi twice hit the mark with a crossbow; he handed Bao an arrow to shoot, and Bao hit three times in four shots.

sentences.zh: 適曰：「今之飛將也。

translations.literal: Shi said: "The flying general of today.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "A flying general of our own day.

sentences.zh: 」神宗稱其勇，以比薛仁貴。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shenzong praised his courage and compared him to Xue Rengui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong praised his courage and compared him to Xue Rengui.

sentences.zh: 及死，厚恤其家。

translations.literal: When he died, his family was generously compensated.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the court gave his family generous relief.

sentences.zh: 論曰：蔚昭敏、高化、周美，蓋皆有功於邊鄙者。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Yu Zhaomin, Gao Hua, and Zhou Mei were all men who had merit on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Yu Zhaomin, Gao Hua, and Zhou Mei were all men who had served the frontier with distinction.

sentences.zh: 化在蜀州，取軍中積材以塞水患，又能平反冤獄，脫人於死，蓋武人之知民事者。

translations.literal: While Hua was at Shuzhou, he took accumulated materials from the army to block flooding, and could also reverse unjust cases and rescue men from death—truly a military man who understood civilian affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at Shuzhou, Hua used accumulated army stores to check flooding, and could also reverse unjust verdicts and rescue men from death—a soldier who understood civilian affairs.

sentences.zh: 美敗夏人，焚族部，城堡砦，未嘗擇便利，而所向輒勝；

translations.literal: Mei defeated the Tangut, burned tribal settlements, castles, and forts, never choosing convenient ground, yet wherever he turned he prevailed;
translations.idiomatic: Mei defeated the Tangut, burned tribal settlements, castles, and forts, never picking easy ground, yet wherever he turned he prevailed;

sentences.zh: 所得祿賜，悉分與麾下，士亦樂為之用，推古良將，何以加此。

translations.literal: All stipends and rewards he received he divided entirely among his subordinates, and the soldiers were also glad to serve him—to compare with fine generals of old, how could one add to this?
translations.idiomatic: Every stipend and reward he received he shared entirely with his men, and they were glad to fight for him; compared with the great generals of old, what more could one ask?

sentences.zh: 閻守恭慕郭進為人，而慷慨自效，起徒步至刺史，其志亦豈小哉。

translations.literal: Yan Shougong admired Guo Jin's character and generously devoted himself; rising from common soldier to prefect, his ambition was surely no small one.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shougong admired Guo Jin's character and gave himself wholeheartedly to service; rising from foot soldier to prefect, his ambition was hardly small.

sentences.zh: 孟元、劉謙、馬懷德、范恪皆經略西鄙，數戰有功。

translations.literal: Meng Yuan, Liu Qian, Ma Huaide, and Fan Ke all held the western frontier and repeatedly won merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yuan, Liu Qian, Ma Huaide, and Fan Ke all held the western frontier and won repeated honors in battle.

sentences.zh: 其初起自卒伍，而能練習民事、招輯散亡，不獨一武夫而已。

translations.literal: Rising at first from the ranks, they could yet practice civilian affairs and recruit and gather the scattered—not mere warriors alone.
translations.idiomatic: Though they had risen from the ranks, they could also manage civilian affairs and gather the scattered populace—they were not mere fighting men.

sentences.zh: 趙振挽強命中，精曉兵機。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhen could draw a strong bow and hit the mark, and was finely versed in military arts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhen could draw a heavy bow and hit his mark, and was finely versed in the art of war.

sentences.zh: 塞門之敗，振擁兵不救，何獨暗於此邪？

translations.literal: At the defeat at Saimen, Zhen held troops but did not rescue—why was he alone blind in this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the defeat at Saimen he held troops back and did not go to the rescue—why was he alone so blind in that?

sentences.zh: 」子珣年少習書史，閱武技，用兵以來，人以為無如珣者。

translations.literal: " His son Zixun, though young, studied books and history and reviewed martial skills; since military campaigns began, people considered none the equal of Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixun, though still young, studied the classics and history and trained in martial skills; since the campaigns began, people considered none his equal.

sentences.zh: 籠竿一戰，西人奔走不暇，從容而拔劉滬於死，英風義烈，何可少哉！

translations.literal: At the battle of Longgan the Westerners fled with no time to spare; with composure he rescued Liu Hu from death—such heroic spirit and lofty righteousness, how could it be slighted!
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Longgan the Westerners fled in disorder; with calm assurance he pulled Liu Hu back from death—such heroic spirit and lofty loyalty, how could it be undervalued!

sentences.zh: 葛懷敏以不用珣計而取敗，珣亦力戰而沒，惜哉！

translations.literal: Ge Huaimin by not employing Zixun's plan brought defeat upon himself, and Zixun also fought to the end and perished—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ge Huaimin brought defeat on himself by refusing Zixun's plan, and Zixun also fought to the end and died—alas!

sentences.zh: 安俊、向寶無多戰功，夏人皆識其名而畏之。

translations.literal: An Jun and Xiang Bao had no great many battle achievements, yet the Tangut all knew their names and feared them.
translations.idiomatic: An Jun and Xiang Bao won no great tally of battle honors, yet the Tangut all knew their names and feared them.

sentences.zh: 張忠區區，較之諸人，未可同日語也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhong was petty and small; compared with these men, he cannot be mentioned in the same breath.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong was a petty man; beside these others he cannot be spoken of in the same breath.
